passages.title: The Shoemaker and the Elves
passages.text:
Once upon a time there were a kind shoemaker and his wife. Sadly, no one bought his shoes and they became poor. They only had a piece of leather to make one last pair of shoes. “We must help the poor shoemaker,” said one of the elves. Then they talked about how to help the shoemaker and his wife. One of the elves said, “How about making beautiful shoes while they are sleeping?” [A]

The clever elves *fluttered into the house through the window of the workshop. They took the leather and soon began cutting, *sewing, and decorating it. Before morning, they finished making the most beautiful pair of shoes in the world and then (3) fly away.

In the morning the shoemaker and his wife were amazed to see the pretty little shoes on the table. They said, “Who made the shoes? They are beautiful!” [B] Soon, a *merchant living in the next town saw the shoes in the shop window and said to the shoemaker, “The shoes are really beautiful. Did you make them?” (4) The shoemaker did not say anything but smiled. The merchant decided to buy them and gave the shoemaker enough money to buy leather for two pairs of shoes. That night the shoemaker left the leather on the table again before going to bed and then the elves returned.

One day the shoemaker said to his wife, “I want to know who are making shoes. We must thank them for their kindness.” [C] They decided to keep *awake that night and hide behind the door to find out who made the shoes for them.

As they waited, finally the elves came into the workshop. They quickly made the shoes, laughing and singing. “We are very lucky. We must give something to them! Their clothes are *torn. Let’s make tiny clothes for them,” said his wife. They both worked hard to make the best clothes and the cutest pair of shoes for the elves and left them on the table. The shoemaker’s wife said to her husband, “Do you think the elves will be pleased with the gifts from us?” “Yes, I think so,” said the shoemaker.

Next night the elves came and they were surprised to see the new clothes. One of the elves said, “(6) This shirt is my (f　　　).” Another elf said, “I want to take these shoes with me.” They danced happily, sang songs and went out of the window carrying clothes and shoes in their hands. They were never seen again. The shoemaker continued to make the best shoes in the town and sold them. He said to his wife, “We must not forget the kind elves.” [D]

passages.title: A Gift from Nature
passages.sourceAttribution: Paul Kurashina, A Gift from Nature (2024)
passages.text:
Mark was a 15-year-old boy who lived in a small village in the southern part of England. (1) He had a parrot (　　　) Goldie and looked after the bird every day.

It was a cold day just after Christmas. Goldie suddenly *coughed. It was very unusual of him but Mark did not worry about him. A few days later Goldie did it again. Mark said to his mother, “Is Goldie okay, Mum? I think he (2) catch a cold.” “Don’t worry. Goldie is a healthy bird,” said Mark’s mother. So Mark decided to wait and see.

Two days passed. Goldie still coughed. Mark asked his mother to take Goldie to a local *veterinarian. After seeing Goldie, the veterinarian said, “I’m sorry. Your bird is in a very bad condition. He will (3) pass away soon.” Mark could not stop crying. He said to himself, “Why does Goldie have to die?” About half an hour later, Goldie took its last breath.

Mark and his mother came back home with Goldie. He was very sad but he thought that he had to do something for Goldie. He then wrapped Goldie’s body in his old T-shirt and (4) *buried it under the apple tree in the garden. Goldie liked to see the apple tree through the windows of the living room when he was alive. Mark spent long sad months. He remembered happy days with Goldie *day in and day out.

One day in April, he saw a *robin in the garden. The robin was flying from one tree to another and looking at Mark. Mark said to the robin, “Hello. Where are you from?” The robin looked at Mark again and flew away.

Next day the robin came back to the garden of Mark’s house. Mark did not know if the robin was *male or *female but he decided to call the bird Daisy. It was a female name. Daisy visited the garden every day. Mark thought that it was a good idea to *feed Daisy. So he went to a pet shop in the village on foot and bought *mealworms. Then he came home and put mealworms in a small *flowerpot.

Next morning Mark looked at the flowerpot and saw nothing inside it. He put mealworms in it again and then Daisy came. (5) ( to / Mark / Daisy / mealworms / was / eating / very / see / glad ). He was standing beside the flowerpot but Daisy did not fly away and ate them. In the evening he said to his parents, “Daisy came and she ate mealworms beside me. It was a very exciting moment.”

Summer came. Mark sometimes remembered Goldie but he was not sad. Daisy visited the garden every day and other birds also came to eat mealworms. Mark’s garden was always full of birds.

In September, Daisy became a friend of Mark’s. She came to eat food on Mark’s hand but she did not sit on his shoulder.

Some weeks passed and winter arrived. Usually most female robins fly to warm countries before winter and Daisy (6) did it, too.

It was getting colder and colder and leaves started to fall. One day in early December, Mark was talking about Daisy with Fred, his friend on their way back home. Mark wanted to show Fred Daisy and he took Fred to his garden. Mark put mealworms on his hand and they waited for Daisy. Half an hour passed. Daisy did not come. They decided to wait for another half an hour. But nothing happened. (7) They (s　　　) doing it.

Next day Mark waited for Daisy with mealworms on his hand but Daisy did not come. He waited for her every day but he could not see her. He thought that she was dead because it was cold. Then Mark spent sad months again.

Spring arrived. One day in April, when Mark was watering plants in the garden, Daisy came back. She also brought her baby robins. Mark was surprised and excited to see them. He called Fred and said to him, “Hi, Fred, I have good news for you. Come and see my garden!” His heart was full of joy.

passages.title: The Owls and the Vine
passages.sourceAttribution: Bedtime Stories For Kids - The Goose and the Fig Tree
passages.text:
There were some big *cedar trees with huge branches in one of the forests in England. A *flock of *owls lived there and they were very happy. But at the roots of the cedar tree, a little *vine was starting to grow.
